units.title: Classify square grids erasable three edges per move
units.statement: A square n×n cell grid permits erasing every edge by repeatedly selecting a cell with at least three remaining edges and erasing exactly three iff n=2 or n≡3,5 (mod 6). The total 2n(n+1) edges force n≡0,2 (mod 3). For n≥3 every boundary cell must be selected. Their combined capacity equals all edges incident to the boundary ring, so those edges are all erased there. In the remaining (n−2)×(n−2) open cell grid, corners cannot be selected and the side cells must alternate selected/unselected, forcing n odd. Sufficiency follows from direct 2×2, 3×3, 5×5 constructions and an explicit six-cell-wide induction frame; its edge ownership pattern is recorded in the private digest notes and verified for many sizes in the generator test.
steps: Use boundary-ring capacity to force alternating inner side cells
Construct valid boards with base patterns and a repeating frame
